newsitem.title: USA: NBC declines to comment on USA Networks buy. [CORRECTED 00:24 GMT 04/12]
newsitem.headline: NBC declines to comment on USA Networks buy. [CORRECTED 00:24 GMT 04/12]

text.p: General Electric Co's NBC unit declined to comment on Tuesday on a report that it is in talks to buy the USA Networks cable channels.

A spokesperson for NBC would not comment on the article which appeared in Advertising Age magazine on Monday, but industry sources said that NBC has not yet made a formal offer for the network, which is jointly owned by Viacom Inc and Seagram Co Ltd.
Industry analysts said such a deal could fetch as much as $3 billion.
"No one on the senior staff has talked to anyone at NBC," a USA Networks spokeswoman said.
Ed Hatch, a broadcast and cable analyst at UBS Securities, said NBC had been close to buying an unidentified cable network for the last several weeks.

USA Networks, available in about 65 million homes and with 1996 revenue of about $800 million (corrects from $80 million), would be a smart choice, he said, even though at $3 billion NBC would pay about 15 times its cash flow. "USA is frequently No. 1 in the ratings and with about $200 million in cash flow, it's a good pick for NBC, which is still a relatively small player," Hatch said.
"USA would give them (NBC) a flagship operation which they could use for more distribution and to spread its costs over other networks," he added.
Last month, Seagram and Viacom were reportedly close to a deal in which Viacom would buy the other half of USA for about $1.4 billion, analysts said.

The companies have been wrangling over ownership of the USA since the summer and late last month terminated settlement talks over the network. Viacom and Seagram officials were not available to comment
